newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Dec 4.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Dec 4.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Wednesday morning:

** Morgan Stanley's director of global strategy Barton Biggs recommends underweighting U.S. stocks and overweighting in Japanese equities and in emerging markets like Russia, Brazil, South Korea and India

** A survey of world mutual fund asset allocations shows Mexico was the favourite destination for global emerging market equity funds this year, followed by South Korea, India, South Africa and Brazil
** The steel sector is likely to remain in the doldrums for most of 1997 as a rise in production capacity at home and abroad may keep steel prices in check, analysts say
** Former finance minister Manmohan Singh says he erred in cutting government investment in power generation by relying too much on the private sector, the Times of India reports

** Money markets are likely to tighten in the second fortnight of December as the third instalment of advance tax payments will flow out of the banking system starting December 15, the Economic Times reports
** The Indian rupee INR= opened steady at 35.73/74 and is seen defensive, dealers say
** India was the weakest performer in the Morgan Stanley Capital International (MSCI) index for emerging markets during November, an MSCI statement said on Tuesday.
Emerging markets which fared poorly during the month
included India (-8.9 percent), Chile (-6.3 percent) and South Africa (-5.6 percent).
** India shares fell in nervous trade on Tuesday, with the Bombay Stock Exchange .BSESN 30-share index diving 53.43 points, or 1.87 percent, to 2,798.0, a new three year low.
** The 50-stock National Stock Exchange .NSEI dropped 10.82 points, or 1.3 percent, to 820.25.
